claims.claim: Exelon's regulated grid sits between rising large-load electricity demand and the transmission/distribution infrastructure required to serve it; signed transmission security agreements and collateral are stronger bridge evidence than an unfiltered data-center queue.

The causal chain remains conditional: committed load must clear siting, transmission/generation availability and regulatory affordability before it becomes durable rate-base growth; successor bottlenecks can therefore migrate from customer demand to grid buildout and generation supply.

causalEdges: large-load demand -> interconnection commitment/collateral -> transmission/distribution investment need -> potential regulated rate-base growth
generation/transmission scarcity -> interconnection delay -> delayed load conversion -> delayed infrastructure returns
affordability/regulatory constraint -> capital-plan moderation -> slower rate-base conversion
falsifiers: Collateralized/signed large-load commitments materially cancel or fail to progress through interconnection milestones.
Required grid investment is not recoverable through regulatory processes at acceptable customer affordability.
unknowns: timing and realized returns for individual large-load projects
current primary-source confirmation of Q2 load figures

claims.claim: The reduction of the broader prospective data-center pipeline is not automatically bearish: it removes speculative projects, but it also demonstrates that headline queue size can overstate realizable demand.

Signed agreements and collateral improve demand quality but do not eliminate execution, regulatory, financing or generation-supply constraints; treating all committed GW as near-term earnings would inflate confidence.

unknowns: incremental capital funding and allowed-return timing
